items.title: Australians caught between homelessness and the law
items.description: For Australians on the brink of homelessness, dilapidated boats have become a way to stave off sleeping on the streets, but many are being removed from these vessels amid a safety crackdown.

items.title: Homeowners face tougher conditions than 1989 era of 17pc interest rates, analysis finds
items.description: Who had it tougher on housing? These stats may put the generational debate to bed.

items.title: Polling whets Labor's appetite for reform
items.description: The slight recovery in Labor's polling shifts assumptions about what's in store for the remainder of this parliamentary term.

items.title: World's biggest porn site puts advertising block on Australian AI empire
items.description: Australian pornography website OurDream has had its advertising suspended by Pornhub after the ABC revealed OurDream's content could include child exploitation material.

items.title: Thai teen's ashes laid to rest by family after alleged murder
items.description: The family of a Thai teenager allegedly killed by an Australian man has placed her cremated ashes to rest at a local Buddhist temple as they seek justice for her murder.

items.title: Live: Kane saves England after DR Congo scare, Senegal leads Belgium
items.description: Harry Kane strikes twice after half time as the Three Lions fight back to defeat DR Congo 2-1 and progress to the Round of 16. Follow live.

items.title: Thousands of survivors of child sexual abuse face looming redress backlog
items.description: At its current processing rate, the scheme will not be able to clear its backlog before it closes.

items.title: Extremists using 'codes' to evade detection online, royal commission hears
items.description: Far-right individuals adopt memes as a way to push "more palatable" antisemitism, which is less likely to be picked up by social media moderators.

items.title: Before and after images show widespread impact of Venezuelan quakes
items.description: Venezuela's devastating earthquakes flattened buildings and coated parts of the northern coast in dust and debris, satellite imagery shows.

items.title: Pat Conroy to announce defence shake-up aimed at cost blowouts
items.description: Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy is set to appeal to the Labor faithful to get behind AUKUS as he announces a defence shake-up targeting wasteful spending.

items.title: Labor MP backs gambling ad bill but says 'much more' needs to be done
items.description: The Coalition, Greens and crossbench are also pushing for changes to the bill, which limits TV and radio ads during certain times and creates an opt-out feature for online platforms.

items.title: Russian daredevils climb Empire State Building to unfurl 'love' banner
items.description: Two Russian daredevils, Angela Nikolau and Vanya Beerkus, claim to be the duo who scaled the 102-storey, 443-metre tower for an apparent show of love and a marriage proposal.

items.title: Calls for Football Australia to enforce restrictions on headers
items.description: With all eyes on the World Cup, Australian football's management of the risks associated with the practice of heading the ball, such as dementia and CTE, is in the spotlight.

items.title: Electric-vehicle buyers wait months for promised cashback
items.description: When Mustansir Milky took the leap and bought a new electric vehicle, he didn't expect to have to fight to get the $5,000 cashback payment he was promised.

items.title: Matthew Flinders's steamy letters reveal a hidden side to the man who named Australia
items.description: Flinders circumnavigated and named Australia. Impressive stuff, but he also wrote many impassioned letters and lived a life full of crushes.

items.title: Jackass began with a gun shot, now its a $500m franchise
items.description: For more than 25 years, prank franchise Jackass has been delighting teens and terrifying parents. Now the gang is heading to the cinemas for what could be their last ride.

items.title: Nobody knows where John Frum first came from, but he is god in this village
items.description: On Vanuatu's Tanna Island, I immerse myself in a culture that worships a shape-shifting spirit known as John Frum.

items.title: As main street shops vanish, could they help solve housing shortages?
items.description: As businesses shut up shop in regional main streets, the government is weighing up whether they could help solve the housing crisis.

items.title: 'Snuck a look': Texts between police sergeant and DV-accused mate exposed
items.description: A NSW Police officer has admitted to unlawfully accessing the force's internal database to locate details about a domestic violence complaint against his friend.

items.title: Police investigate death of teenage boy found outside Melbourne hospital
items.description: The boy was found by emergency services workers with serious injuries outside a medical centre in Craigieburn, but died at the scene.

items.title: Spider venom to target 'super mites' killing Australia's honey bees
items.description: Queensland researchers are testing novel ways to kill varroa mites, which have developed a resistance to standard treatments.

items.title: Traditional owner takes government to court over flood plain project
items.description: A protest camp on the banks of the Murray River enters its sixth week as traditional owners and locals fight a plan to return water to nine flood plains they say will kill trees and wildlife.

items.title: French Open champ Mirra Andreeva left in tears after early Wimbledon exit
items.description: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva is reduced to tears after her Wimbledon run is ended in the second round by former winner Barbora Krejčíková.

items.title: This 8yo is one of many girls and young women driving golf numbers up
items.description: Women are taking up golf nearly twice as fast as men, with junior golfers like Rianna Hills one of many young people giving the sport a huge participation boost.

items.title: Karl Stefanovic to be dumped from radio show, defends 'legitimate interview'
items.description: Karl Stefanovic will be dumped from his new radio show amid fallout from his interview with Tommy Robinson, the ABC understands.
